$comment: THE FILTER WIRE, AS A TABLE. Byte-identical copies of this file live in
Each implementation drives its own parser from it, which is the only thing that turns
'the Laravel, Node and browser halves speak one grammar' from a claim in a docblock
into something a test fails on. If you change a case here, change it in every copy —
and if you cannot make every copy pass, the wire has forked and that is the bug.
`offered` is the operator allow-list the filter declared; `operator` is the EFFECTIVE
operator (a request that names none reads as `is`); `values` are what remains after the

cases.name: a bare value is equality, exactly as before the wire existed
the operator rides on the whole filter, not on a value
an operator the filter did not declare is part of the value
an unknown token is part of the value
a hostile prefix is inert text, never an operator
a value that merely contains a colon filters for itself
only the FIRST colon is considered
the filter's own default is always nameable, so a client can switch back
empty elements are dropped, so a stray comma is not a filter for nothing
a lone comma carries no value at all
an operator with nothing after it carries no value at all
an empty parameter carries no value at all
a comparison operator is read where the filter declares one
a partial operator is read where the filter declares one
